## Statement

Systems now translate trial descriptions into cohort definitions or analysis code, and natural language processing extracts eligibility information from unstructured notes. The failure mode of these systems is not that they crash. It is that they silently substitute a different estimand: mistranslating a temporal condition, resolving an ambiguous eligibility phrase to the wrong operationalization, or emitting code that is syntactically valid and causally invalid. None of these failures is visible in the output, which is a working pipeline returning a plausible number. What is missing is a validation regime that treats generated code as an untrusted artifact rather than as a productivity gain.

## Why it is open

Temporal logic is where these systems fail and where testing is hardest: the difference between treatment before eligibility assessment and treatment after it is one word in the specification and one join condition in the code, and both readings execute. There is no reference answer to test against, because the correct cohort is precisely what the pipeline was built to produce. Evaluating on downstream effect estimates is circular, since a wrong cohort with a plausible effect passes.

## What has been tried

::: {.table-scroll}

| Work | What it contributes |
|---|---|
| [Kim, et al. From study design to executable code: automating target trial emulation with large language models. JAMIA Open 2026](https://doi.org/10.1093/jamiaopen/ooag131) | Builds the translation from study design to executable emulation code, which is the system whose failure modes this problem concerns. |
| [Wang, et al. An operational target trial emulation framework for causal inference using electronic health records. npj Digit Med 2026](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41746-026-02563-z) | Specifies the operational mapping from protocol component to record-level definition, which is the interface a compiler would have to respect. |

:::

## Probable solution or research direction

Treat automation as a constrained compiler with three stages: a human-authored causal specification, a typed intermediate representation, and data-source-specific code generated from it. Require unit tests over synthetic test patients constructed so that each temporal condition has a patient that distinguishes the correct reading from the plausible wrong one, plus temporal-logic validation of the intermediate representation. Require dual human sign-off on the specification and on the generated cohort counts, and publish both, so the artifact under review is the specification rather than the number.

## Verification

::: {.verification-trail}
**Verdict.** Confirmed open. Auditors found the problem open. At least one qualified how it is stated; the qualification and who made it are in the trail below.

**Dissent.** literature dissented (supported): Automated translation from study design to executable emulation code exists, and agentic authoring of OMOP concept sets from natural language is now being attempted, so the systems the entry describes are real and multiplying. [...]

4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check
:   **open / supported.** Automated translation from study design to executable emulation code exists, and agentic authoring of OMOP concept sets from natural language is now being attempted, so the systems the entry describes are real and multiplying. Nothing in the corpus supplies the validation regime the entry asks for: no typed intermediate representation, no temporal-logic validation, no synthetic test patients constructed to distinguish the correct reading of a temporal condition from the plausible wrong one, and no dual sign-off requirement. The gap between capability and validation is the claim, and the corpus shows only the capability half.
    Cites 10.1093/jamiaopen/ooag131: Builds the translation the entry is concerned about, which establishes the capability without supplying the validation..
    Cites 10.64898/2026.06.02.26354704: Extends automation to phenotype definition, which is the component where a silent error changes the cohort..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens
:   **open / overstated.** Executable code can silently change eligibility, time zero, assignment, follow-up, or the resulting estimand, so the core risk is real. However, it is false that such errors are necessarily invisible or that no reference answer can exist. Independently authored specifications, expert-labeled records, hand-coded reference implementations, differential testing, and synthetic boundary-case patients can provide component-level or end-to-end reference answers. The report's own proposed synthetic-patient tests contradict the categorical no-reference-answer claim. Agreement of a downstream effect estimate is insufficient evidence of semantic correctness, but evaluating against an external randomized benchmark is not literally circular. Typed intermediate representations and temporal tests reduce risk without proving semantic equivalence for every real-world mapping. No package capability claim is present.

Grok 4.5, recency lens
:   **open / supported.** Kim et al. (JAMIA Open 2026; THESEUS) and Wang et al. (npj Digit Med 2026) build or specify automated protocol-to-code and operational EHR mappings; they are the systems whose silent estimand-shift risk the problem names, not fixes of that risk. Lee et al. (JMIR Med Inform 2025) validate LLM-generated trial-criteria queries for functional correctness, which is partial operational testing but not temporal-logic unit tests that distinguish treatment-before versus treatment-after eligibility. Girshovitz, Zeltzer, and Gilad-Bachrach (arXiv:2607.21173, 2026) propose ARA: structured protocol intermediate form, SCM synthetic failure scenarios, and adversarial validation so that silent success is replaced by visible protocol or diagnostic failure. That is closely aligned with the report direction, yet it is a proposal with a small econometric-style benchmark; it does not establish a standard validation regime for TTE automation, dual human sign-off on specification and cohort counts, or synthetic patients that isolate each temporal join. Guidance (TARGET 2025 reporting; FDA/EMA RWE documents) addresses transparency of human-designed emulations, not untrusted machine-generated code. No CRAN or GitHub merge was found that ships a constrained TTE compiler with temporal unit tests. Silent estimand substitution under syntactically valid pipelines remains open.

GLM-5.2, third independent lens
:   **open / supported.** The claim is internally consistent and correctly identifies the silent estimand substitution as a structural risk in automated translation. The reasons given for it being open (lack of reference answers, circularity of downstream evaluation) strongly support the claim. The scope is appropriate and the severity is proportionate to the cost of a wrong estimand.

Decision path
:   `R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex`

:::
